text:
maria: heads up — new customer AstraLyft can't find their API credentials after SSO. console shows no api key, they get a 403 when calling /v1/generate

sam: thanks, any repro steps or account id?

maria: they signed up via Okta SSO, got to the project page, clicked 'Create API key' — UI showed success but client never received key. customer id: acct_az12.

josh: looking at provisioner logs for acct_az12 — I can see a key object created but it's attached to project `internal-tools`. snippet from logs: ```json
{"key_id":"k_01a7f2","created_by":"provisioner","account":"acct_az12","project":"internal-tools","status":"active"}
```

maria: whoa that's wrong — should be bound to their customer project (proj_az12).

sam: can you paste the provisioner run id? I want to correlate with the SSO callback.

josh: run id r-2024-09-12-07. Provisioner emitted no errors. Looks like claim routing matched an internal project tag during binding. suspect org-policy mapping or a tag collision in the provisioner catalog.

maria: customer is blocked. they tried calling the API and got: ```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{ "error": "project_mismatch", "detail": "key not valid for requested project" }
```

infra-bot: deploy-notice: provisioner v2.11 rolled out 2024-09-11 03:14 UTC, flagging for trace: routing-tag-fix not enabled on canary hosts.

sam: possible race: canary hosts still had old mapping so key was created against fallback project. If so, rebind should fix it. josh — can you run admin rebind?

josh: about to run: `rwd-admin rebind-key --key-id k_01a7f2 --to-project proj_az12 --audit "support:1749991234"`

josh: done — rebind returned success and I invalidated old key and issued a new visible key in the customer's console. reply from admin: ```
{"status":"rebound","key_id":"k_01a7f2","new_project":"proj_az12","issued_key":"sk_live_az_7f2x"}
```

maria: forwarded new key to customer via secure link, they confirmed calls succeed. :party-parrot:

sam: created follow-up ticket to force consistency check across all provisioner canaries and added a short-term alert for routing-tag drift. ticket: #SUP-2024-981

josh: pushing a config roll to the remaining canaries now. will monitor.

maria: thanks team — closing this thread once monitoring shows no more misbindings.

sam: noted: root cause likely mix of canary config + tag collision in the routing map. next steps: (1) full memcache flush of provisioner routing table, (2) add unit test for tag precedence, (3) backfill audit entries for any keys created in window 2024-09-11T03:00-04:00Z.

maria: adding customer note to ticket: they were given a new key, apologized for the disruption, and we documented a temp mitigation to manually rebind if seen again.

infra-bot: incident-bot: monitoring alert cleared for provisioner-routing-drift at 2024-09-12T08:12:09Z.
